gloss: small token of gratitude (money or gift); gratuity

definitions.gloss: small token of gratitude; gratuity; small gift of money
definitions.explanation: A humble term for a small gift — typically a modest sum of cash in a special envelope — given as a token of gratitude, appreciation, or good wishes. Used when the giver wants to downplay the value of what they are offering.

examples.japanese: {寸志|すんし}をお{渡|わた}しした。
examples.english: I gave a small gift of money.

examples.japanese: {封筒|ふうとう}に「{寸志|すんし}」と{書|か}いて{渡|わた}した。
examples.english: I wrote "a small token" on the envelope and handed it over.

examples.japanese: お{世話|せわ}になった{先生|せんせい}に{寸志|すんし}として{商品券|しょうひんけん}をお{贈|おく}りした。
examples.english: I gave a gift voucher as a small token of thanks to the teacher who helped me.

examples.japanese: {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}で{上司|じょうし}から{寸志|すんし}が{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: At the welcome-and-farewell party, a small monetary contribution was collected from the superiors.

notes:
A humble word composed of {寸|すん} (a small unit of length; "a bit") + {志|し} (intention, will, feeling). Literally "a tiny bit of feeling," it is used by the giver to modestly describe their own gift — never by the recipient to describe what they received. Most often refers to a small amount of cash, though it can also refer to a small object like a voucher or box of sweets.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寸志|すんし}を{贈|おく}る: to give a small token
- {寸志|すんし}をお{渡|わた}しする: to present a small token (humble)
- {寸志|すんし}として: as a small token
- 「{寸志|すんし}」と{書|か}く: to write "a small token" (on an envelope)
- {御|ご}{寸志|すんし}: honorific form, used on an envelope

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{心付|こころづ}け: tip, gratuity — often given directly for services, e.g., to staff at a ryokan
- お{礼|れい}: expression of thanks; a thank-you gift — broader; includes both gifts and words of thanks
- {御|ご}{祝儀|しゅうぎ}: celebratory gift money — used for weddings, promotions, and festive occasions
- {薄謝|はくしゃ}: modest honorarium — similar humble self-descriptive term, more formal

USAGE:
{寸志|すんし} is the standard word written on the envelope when senior employees or supervisors contribute money to an event (such as a party or travel fund) where their contribution is voluntary and separate from the main collection. It is never used by the receiver to describe what they were given, as doing so would sound ungrateful or rude.
